I could not verify this computationally here, so my judgment relies on recalling the literature. The problem is the high school identities (HSI) setting. The listed identities are the HSI axioms, and the inequality is the failure of Wilkie's identity. Burris and Yeats ("The saga of the high school identities") are, as I recall, the source for the claim that 12 is the minimum size of a finite HSI algebra violating Wilkie's identity, with exactly two such algebras up to isomorphism. I'm fairly but not fully confident in that recollection, and none of the three solutions shows a complete enumeration.

Solutions 1 and 2 both give 2. Solution 2 admits it did not finish the classification and leans on the same literature claim, with some extra details I can't confirm, such as the attribution of the 59-element example. Solution 3 is an explicit guess from memory. Since 2 matches the recalled result, Solution 1 is the cleanest correct-answer candidate.

CHOICE: 1
